"""Explain p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4224 with a position-in-document drift.

This component has no firing pattern: its causal importance is essentially zero at
every token, and switching it off changes the model's output by almost nothing. Its
activation is a noisy value around zero (std 0.28). The one readable regularity is a
drift with position inside the document: the first token sits at a fixed value, the
second token is clearly negative, and the value then drifts up slowly (roughly
linearly in the log of the position) and is about zero to slightly positive deep into
a document. This program predicts that drift and nothing else.
"""

import math

READS = ()

FIRST_TOKEN = -0.008  # the first token of a document: a fixed value
SECOND_TOKEN = -0.25  # the second token: clearly negative


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document label, index of the newest token within its document)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        k = 0  # first token of a new document
    else:
        k = carry[1] + 1
    if k == 0:
        value = FIRST_TOKEN
    elif k == 1:
        value = SECOND_TOKEN
    else:
        value = -0.146 + 0.024 * math.log2(k)
    return (doc, k), value

"""Position-in-document trend of one weak MLP down-projection component (layer 15).

This component is diffuse: its activation has mean about 0.14 and spread about 0.36, and no
token identity, character class or repetition explains it. The only reliable structure is
where the token sits in its document:

- the first token of each document gives 0 (the activation there is always about 0);
- the second token gives a fairly large value (about 0.5), and the value falls off as the
  position grows, settling near 0.12 deep into a document.

So the program predicts 0 at a document's first token and 0.12 + 0.5 / position elsewhere.
It explains only about 1% of the variance; the rest is the component's own noise.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document label, position of the previous token), or None at a row's start.
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or doc != carry[0]:
        pos = 0
    else:
        pos = carry[1] + 1
    value = 0.0 if pos == 0 else 0.12 + 0.5 / pos
    return (doc, pos), value


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # A quick check on a made-up document: positions 0..4 give 0, 0.62, 0.37, 0.287, 0.245.
    class P:
        document_ids = [7]
    carry = None
    for k in range(5):
        P.document_ids = [7] * (k + 1)
        carry, v = step(carry, P, {})
        print(k, round(v, 3))

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 4226 (this component is that unit's activation, scaled by ~1.1).

The unit is a dense, context-driven signal. Its value depends on the residual stream in ways
no token list or simple context rule captures: token identity, the previous token, position in
the document, column in a line, the model's own entropy and surprisal all leave most of the
variance unexplained. What simple readable tendencies do show is in the current token's text:

- a run of padding whitespace (two or more spaces, tabs, or no-break spaces, as in aligned
  tables and indentation) pulls it negative;
- a lone space token pulls it negative;
- a token that is only part of a multi-byte character (decodes to U+FFFD) pulls it slightly
  positive;
- anything else sits near zero.

The program predicts the average activation of each of these classes. It is a faithful
summary of those tendencies, not an explanation of the unit's large swings.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

PADDING_RUN = -0.11  # two or more whitespace characters in one token
LONE_SPACE = -0.07  # a single space token
UTF8_FRAGMENT = 0.06  # a part of a multi-byte character
OTHER = 0.02  # everything else


def predict(text: str) -> float:
    """The class mean for one token's text."""
    if "�" in text:
        return UTF8_FRAGMENT
    plain = text.replace("\xa0", " ")
    if "\n" not in plain and plain and not plain.strip():
        return PADDING_RUN if len(plain) >= 2 else LONE_SPACE
    return OTHER


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """Predict this component's activation at the newest token from that token's text."""
    return None, predict(prefix.token_strings[-1])

"""Component 4227 of layer 15's MLP down projection, as a word-start token rule.

The component's activation is a weighted sum of a few MLP hidden units (mostly units
4227, 4974 and 3302). Those units are spiky and depend on context, and no short rule
tracks them: the component's activation is mostly unexplained by the token at each
position. The one thing a short rule captures is its tendency on words:

- a word-start token (leading space) that is a broken UTF-8 fragment (decodes to
  U+FFFD) or a CJK / kana fragment is strongly negative (-2.2);
- other word-start tokens are slightly positive if they are common English words
  (+0.14) and slightly negative otherwise (-0.1);
- tokens that continue a word, or are digits and punctuation, are 0;
- the first token of each document is 0.

On eval rows this explains about 0% of the activation's variance (correlation 0.10).
Put into the model in place of the component, it is slightly better than switching the
component off: KL 0.97 of switching-off's, cross entropy 6e-5 against 9e-5 nats per token.
The continuation and punctuation classes add about 1% of variance, but they make the
model's next-token cross entropy worse than switching off, so they are left out.
"""

import regex

READS = ()
"""No other component's program feeds this one."""

COMMON_WORDS = set(
    "the of and to a in is it that for on with as was at by this be from or an are not "
    "have has had but his her they you we he she their which one all were there can more "
    "if no when out so up said about into than other its some what who will would just".split()
)
"""A small list of the most frequent English words."""

BROKEN_OR_CJK = r"[\p{Han}\p{Hiragana}\p{Katakana}\p{Hangul}]"
"""Characters from scripts whose word fragments the component reads as strongly negative."""


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    first_in_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if first_in_doc or not text.startswith(" "):
        return carry, 0.0
    fragment = "�" in text or regex.search(BROKEN_OR_CJK, text) is not None
    if fragment:
        return carry, -2.2
    if text.strip().lower() in COMMON_WORDS:
        return carry, 0.14
    return carry, -0.1

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4228 (p-82af68dd).

What it does: almost nothing that a reader can name. Its activation is a diffuse readout of
layer 15's MLP hidden state (mostly hidden unit 3125, plus 4228 and hundreds of small ones),
with a spread of about 0.22 around a mean of about -0.01. Its value is not set by the token:
a per-token lookup explains under 3% of its variance even when fitted on held-out rows. It is
not set by the position in the document either. It never passes the causal-importance
threshold, and switching it off moves the model's next-token predictions by about 1e-6 nats.

So the program predicts the component's typical value everywhere, and 0 at the first token of
each document, where the component is silent (its activation there is ~0 in every sample).
"""

READS = ()

TYPICAL_VALUE = -0.01
"""The component's average activation over ordinary tokens."""


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # The first token of a row, or of a document inside it, has no earlier context.
    first = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    return carry, 0.0 if first else TYPICAL_VALUE

"""Weak, mostly-unexplained predictor for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 4229.

What the component is: a rank-one readout of MLP hidden unit 4229 in layer 15 (its
output direction is about 0.58 times that unit's value). Its activation is near zero
almost everywhere (std 0.33), with rare large values. Its output promotes words such as
"thus", "therefore" and "因此", a sign that it helps write consequence-style text.

Where it is high (up to about 8): at the word that starts the consequence of a cause,
condition or change, in explanatory prose. Examples: "lead[ to]", "causes [the]",
"if b > a, [then]", "when the volume increases[,] the", "moves [the rack]".
Where it is low (down to about -6): in arithmetic and bookkeeping text ("for a total
of", "=", digits) and in code or tool-call markup.

This program captures only that coarse picture: it adds a bump when a consequence
word (then, lead, cause, increase, therefore, ...) appears in the last three tokens of
the same document, dips slightly when digits or code symbols appear in the last six,
and otherwise predicts a small constant. Its variance explained is only about 0.2%,
because the component's activation depends on context that no word list captures;
a bag of the 600 most common words in the window reaches about 0.8% on held-out rows.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping
import re

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Words that introduce a consequence, a result or a change.
CONSEQUENCE = {
    "then", "lead", "leads", "led", "cause", "causes", "caused", "causing",
    "induce", "induces", "implies", "result", "results", "resulted",
    "therefore", "thus", "hence", "increase", "increases", "decrease",
    "decreases", "becomes", "means",
}

# Digits, and symbols common in arithmetic and code.
BOOKKEEPING = re.compile(r"\d|[=<>{}();\[\]]")

BASE = -0.025  # the component's typical (mean) value
CONSEQUENCE_BUMP = 0.10
BOOKKEEPING_DIP = -0.02


def _window(prefix, size):
    """The last `size` tokens' text, lowercased and stripped, within the same document."""
    t = prefix.position
    doc = prefix.document_ids[t]
    words = []
    for i in range(t, max(-1, t - size), -1):
        if prefix.document_ids[i] != doc:
            break
        words.append(prefix.token_strings[i].strip().lower())
    return words


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    recent = _window(prefix, 3)
    value = BASE
    if any(word in CONSEQUENCE for word in recent):
        value += CONSEQUENCE_BUMP
    if any(BOOKKEEPING.search(word) for word in _window(prefix, 6)):
        value += BOOKKEEPING_DIP
    return carry, value

"""Component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4230, read as an "exit / error branch" feature.

Its activation is small and noisy almost everywhere, with large tails. The tails
have a readable pattern:

- Strongly negative on exit-like words (exit, abort, terminate, panic, raise,
  throw, quit) when an error or failure word was seen in the last few dozen tokens,
  i.e. inside an error-handling branch that is about to leave the function or program.
  Also negative on `return` in that context.
- Mildly negative on indentation that starts a line in such a context: the model
  is about to write the exit or return statement.
- Positive on `else` and on the token right after it (the `{` or `:` that opens the branch).

Everything else gets the component's typical small negative value.
"""

import re

READS = ()

ERROR_WORD = re.compile(r"error|fail|invalid|not found|usage|warn|cannot|unable|unsupported|wrong|missing", re.I)
EXIT_WORD = re.compile(r"exit|abort|terminat|panic|quit|raise|throw|fatal", re.I)
WINDOW = 25  # tokens an error word stays "recent"
BASE = -0.03  # typical activation


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if prefix.position > 0 else ""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry["doc"] != doc:
        carry = {"doc": doc, "recent": 0}
    in_error = carry["recent"] > 0
    word = tok.strip()

    if EXIT_WORD.search(tok):
        value = -2.1 if in_error else -0.3
    elif word == "return":
        value = -0.7 if in_error else -0.1
    elif not word and "\n" in prev:
        value = -0.6 if in_error else -0.14
    elif "else" in tok:
        value = 0.35
    elif "else" in prev:
        value = 0.8
    else:
        value = BASE

    if ERROR_WORD.search(tok):
        carry["recent"] = WINDOW
    else:
        carry["recent"] = max(0, carry["recent"] - 1)
    return carry, float(value)

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 4231 (this component's input direction is that unit alone),
read as a 'removal / teardown' detector.

The unit's output pushes the next-token guess toward words like delete, remove, cancel, clear,
stop and revoke. It is most active in code and prose about removing, deleting, cancelling,
clearing, closing or releasing something. This program therefore predicts a small positive
value on a removal-type word and for a few tokens after it, and the resting value elsewhere.
Its predictions are small: most of the unit's variance is not captured by surface words.
"""
import re

READS = ()

REMOVAL = re.compile(
    r"(delet|remov|cancel|clear|clean|stop|clos|free|unlink|revok|reset|kill|destroy|erase|"
    r"releas|lock|dispos|uninstall|disconnect|purge|discard|withdraw|abort|terminat|shutdown|"
    r"detach|unload|drop|wipe|undo|revert|forget|\brm\b|\bdel\b)",
    re.I,
)
REST = -0.04  # the unit's typical value
WINDOW = 4    # tokens after a removal word that still count as its context


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """carry: (document label, position of the last removal word in that document)."""
    doc, t = prefix.document_ids[-1], prefix.position
    last = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else -10**9
    if REMOVAL.search(prefix.token_strings[-1]):
        last = t
    gap = t - last
    if gap == 0:
        value = 0.2   # the removal word itself
    elif gap <= WINDOW:
        value = 0.09  # just after one
    else:
        value = REST
    return (doc, last), value

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 4232, as seen through component 4232 of layers.15.mlp.down_proj.

Almost all of this component's read is the MLP hidden unit 4232 of layer 15 (its input
direction V_c is about 70% that one unit). Its value is near zero on most tokens, and it
swings hard negative (down to about -26) on a sparse set of context-dependent tokens: a
repeated name, a letter standing for a variable in a formula, a number in a list. Those
spikes are not explained by the token's surface form, so this program does not try to
find them.

What it does: a flat, weak, signed guess by surface type of the current token.
- punctuation and whitespace: a little below zero (they average about -0.01);
- digits and non-ASCII tokens (accented letters, CJK): more negative (about -0.065);
- every other word-like token: about -0.04.
This is the average pattern the data shows, not a mechanism.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

PUNCT_VALUE = -0.01
WORD_VALUE = -0.04
MARKED_VALUE = -0.065


def _is_punct(text: str) -> bool:
    """Whitespace or only non-alphanumeric characters."""
    text = text.strip()
    return text == "" or all(not ch.isalnum() for ch in text)


def _is_marked(text: str) -> bool:
    """A digit token, or one with a non-ASCII character."""
    text = text.strip()
    return text.isdigit() or any(ord(ch) > 127 for ch in text)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """The component's activation at the current token: a weak surface-type average."""
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if _is_punct(token):
        value = PUNCT_VALUE
    elif _is_marked(token):
        value = MARKED_VALUE
    else:
        value = WORD_VALUE
    return carry, value

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4233: no describable pattern, so predict a constant.

This component's activation is a diffuse, sign-changing value with mean about 0 and
standard deviation about 0.31. It is not tied to any token, token class, position or
document feature we could find: a per-token lookup, a character-class model and a
causal running-context model each explain under 2% of its variance on held-out
training text. It reads the layer-15 MLP hidden state spread over many units (its
largest single input is hidden unit 4233 itself, correlation 0.28), so it has no
short human-level rule.

The program therefore predicts the component's typical value everywhere: 0.
Its contribution to the model is negligible (switching it off changes the next-token
distribution by about 1e-6 nats per position), so a constant is the honest summary.
"""

READS = ()

TYPICAL_ACTIVATION = 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Return the carry unchanged and the constant activation for this position."""
    return carry, TYPICAL_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP unit 4234, as seen through its down_proj component `4234`.

The component reads almost entirely from one MLP hidden unit (layer 15, unit 4234; weight 0.9
of its input direction), so its activation is roughly that unit's value. Most of the time it
is small, diffuse noise around zero, with no token identity that explains it (a per-token mean
explains under 0.1% of its variance, and a linear model on the last 8 tokens about 1%).

Two word-level cues move it clearly, and this program predicts only those:

- Negative on a word about adding or inserting into a collection ("add", "Add", ".add",
  "added", "insert", "append"). Read through the unembedding, the component's output
  promotes add-words when its activation is negative (a logit lens); the activation does not
  track how likely the model finds "add" next.
- Positive on a path-root slash, as in `cd /workspace` or `"/testbed/...`.

Everything else gets the component's mean, about zero. This explains only a sliver of the
variance: most of the activation, and most of its large negative values, has no such cue.
"""

import re

ADD_WORD = re.compile(r"(?i)(add|insert|append)")
PATH_SLASH = {"/", " /", ' "/', '"/', "'/", " '/", "`/", " `/"}
ADD_VALUE = -0.55
PATH_VALUE = 0.25
BASE = 0.025


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if prefix.position == 0 or new_doc:
        return carry, 0.0
    if ADD_WORD.search(text):
        return carry, ADD_VALUE
    if text in PATH_SLASH:
        return carry, PATH_VALUE
    return carry, BASE


READS = ()

"""p-82af68dd layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4235 as a readable rule.

This component is almost entirely MLP hidden unit 4235 of layer 15 (its one
large input weight). Its activation is usually near zero and goes strongly
negative in two kinds of text:

1. Verse and song lyrics. Lines are short (about 4 to 10 words) and start with
   a capital letter, and the text runs on line after line. Inside such a poem,
   words that open a phrase ("his", "my", "their", "the", "in", "to") push the
   activation down.
2. Long unbroken strings of letters and digits, such as base64 or hashes.
   Inside a run of 32 or more such characters the activation is negative.

Everywhere else it sits near zero. The rule is a rough sketch: most of the
variance is in small, diffuse values that no short rule captures.
"""

import string

READS = ()

PHRASE_OPENERS = frozenset(
    "his her my your their our its the a an this that these those "
    "of in on to from by with for at into upon over under and or".split()
)
RUN_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "+/=")
RUN_LENGTH = 32
STRENGTH = 0.5
"""Shrinks every rule toward zero: the rules explain little, so full strength overshoots."""


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry["doc"] != doc:
        carry = {"doc": doc, "verse": 0.0, "words": 0, "capital": False, "run": 0}
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = text.strip()

    # Length of the current run of base64-like characters.
    if word and not text.startswith(" ") and all(c in RUN_CHARS for c in word):
        carry["run"] += len(word)
    else:
        carry["run"] = 0

    # Verse: each finished line of 4 to 10 words that starts with a capital
    # nudges a running score toward 1; other lines nudge it toward 0.
    if "\n" in text:
        if carry["words"] > 0:
            fits = 4 <= carry["words"] <= 10 and carry["capital"]
            carry["verse"] = 0.75 * carry["verse"] + 0.25 * fits
        carry["words"], carry["capital"] = 0, False
        word = text.split("\n")[-1].strip()
    if word:
        if carry["words"] == 0:
            carry["capital"] = word[0].isupper()
        if carry["words"] == 0 or text.startswith(" "):
            carry["words"] += 1

    value = -0.15 * carry["verse"]
    if carry["run"] >= RUN_LENGTH:
        value -= 0.6
    if text.startswith(" ") and word.lower() in PHRASE_OPENERS:
        value -= 0.4 * carry["verse"]
    return carry, float(STRENGTH * value)

"""Digits written inside arithmetic: a negative push on digits in math-dense text.

Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4236 is one rank-one piece of the
layer-15 MLP's down projection. Its activation is near zero on almost every token, but
on digit tokens it swings strongly, and the swings are mostly negative. Which way it
swings depends on the surrounding text: digits in calculations (decimal numbers, sums,
ratios, equations) go strongly negative, while digits in ordinary prose stay near zero.

This program predicts that from the text alone:
  - Only a digit token gets a nonzero prediction; every other token predicts 0.
  - For a digit, count the arithmetic symbols among the 64 tokens before it, in the same
    document: + - * / = ^ ( ) x ≈ − and the decimal point.
  - More such symbols means a more negative activation, linearly: about -0.25 per symbol,
    starting from +0.46 when there are none.
"""

READS = ()

DIGITS = set("0123456789")
ARITHMETIC = set("+-*/=^()×≈−.")
WINDOW = 64  # tokens looked back over, within the same document
BASE = 0.46  # activation on a digit with no arithmetic nearby
PER_SYMBOL = -0.25  # change per arithmetic symbol in the window


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    if prefix.token_strings[t] not in DIGITS:
        return carry, 0.0
    symbols = 0
    for i in range(max(0, t - WINDOW), t):
        if prefix.document_ids[i] == prefix.document_ids[t] and prefix.token_strings[i].strip() in ARITHMETIC:
            symbols += 1
    return carry, BASE + PER_SYMBOL * symbols

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj component 4237: a weak word-class predictor.

The component is one rank-one piece of layer 15's MLP output. Its activation is
(hidden activation . V) times the norm of U; about 29% of its variance comes from MLP hidden
unit 4237 alone. The activation is usually small and slightly positive (median about +0.06),
with sparse large negative excursions (down to about -10). Those excursions are not
predicted by token identity, the next token, position, line position, or the model's own
confidence. Lookup tables over the current token explain about 2% of its variance on
held-out rows, over the last two or three tokens about 3 to 4%, and character-class
n-grams under 1%.

This program keeps the coarse tendencies that are visible in the data:
- Words that frame a choice or a condition ("if", "case", "first", "either", "latter",
  "before", "unlike", "without", "one", "when", "otherwise") sit lower, about -0.07 on
  average. The strongest dips are on "First", "If" and "case".
- Linking words and equals signs ("was", "is", "were", "or", "=", "->", "did") sit higher,
  about +0.14.
- Digits sit a little above baseline, about +0.07.
- Every other token sits at the baseline, about +0.05.

Measured on 1024 eval rows it explains about 0.1% of the variance (Pearson r 0.04); a
constant predictor explains none. Its main value is to show what the component does not
respond to.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

FRAMING = {
    "if", "case", "first", "either", "latter", "before", "unlike", "without",
    "one", "when", "otherwise",
}
LINKING = {"was", "is", "were", "or", "=", "->", "did"}
MEANS = {"framing": -0.07, "linking": 0.14, "digit": 0.07, "other": 0.05}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if word in FRAMING:
        value = MEANS["framing"]
    elif word in LINKING:
        value = MEANS["linking"]
    elif word.isdigit():
        value = MEANS["digit"]
    else:
        value = MEANS["other"]
    return carry, value

"""Component L15 MLP down_proj:4238: a "concrete physical description" feature.

The component goes negative on words that describe physical space and the body in it: where
things are and how they are posed, shaped, oriented or moved ("located", "situated",
"sitting", "standing", "mounted", "vertical", "curved", "narrow", "nearby", "walking",

"distance", "large", "thin", "left", "north", "edge", "room", "village") and on body parts,

other nouns and adjectives barely so.

Each token is classed by its word, with WordNet supplying the base form, so "sitting" and
"sit" count alike. Each class's value is about the mean activation measured on training text.
The program keeps no state: it reads only the newest token.

CARRY_WEIGHT = -0.07  # value added per unit of carried topic


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """Predict the activation at the newest token of `prefix`."""
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    score = 0.0 if (carry is None or new_doc) else carry
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    hit = 1.0 if (SEEK.search(word) or ASK.search(word)) else 0.0
    value = BASE
    if SEEK.search(word):
        value = SEEK_VALUE
    elif ASK.search(word):
        value = ASK_VALUE
    value += CARRY_WEIGHT * score
    return DECAY * score + hit, float(value)

"""Predict the typical activation of layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4274, zero at each row's first token.

What the component does: it is a dense, weak readout of layer 15's MLP hidden units. Its
activation sits near -0.074 at ordinary tokens, with a spread (std about 0.27) that no simple
concept accounts for: the token's class (letter, digit, punctuation, space), its position,
its neighbours' classes, and whether a token repeats earlier text each explain well under 1%
of the variance, and a per-token-identity table only about 4%. The first token of each row
has an activation of about 0 (the model's attention has nothing before it), and the program
reflects that.

So this program predicts the mean everywhere, except 0 at a row's first position. Its
variance explained is about zero: that is the honest level of what a short readable rule can
capture here.
"""

READS = ()

TYPICAL_ACTIVATION = -0.074
FIRST_POSITION_ACTIVATION = 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if prefix.position == 0:
        return carry, FIRST_POSITION_ACTIVATION
    return carry, TYPICAL_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 4275 (the component's input direction is almost
entirely this unit), read as a "difficulty is coming" detector.

Its activation is mostly negative. Pushed through the unembedding, its output
(the negative direction) promotes words such as "difficult", "complex",
"complicated", "challenging", "lack", "limited", "unclear", "impossible".
So it goes negative where the model expects a word of difficulty, complexity
or limitation next. It is strongest on the words just before such a word and
in passages already discussing problems; it is near zero elsewhere.

Honest scope: these few word classes explain only a small share of its
variance (about 0.5% on eval). Most of the variance sits in rare, large
negative spikes that depend on context no word list captures. The program
gets the sign and the rough size of the typical response, not the spikes.

This program mirrors that with a few plain word classes:
  - the current token is itself a difficulty word          -> strongly negative
  - the current token is a connective that sets up a problem ("but", "because",
    "however", ...), or a copula/modal ("is", "are", "may", ...) -> mildly negative
  - a decaying count of difficulty words in the preceding text -> more negative
  - otherwise a small constant negative offset.
Positions reset at each document boundary, as the model does.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

DIFFICULTY = set(
    "difficult difficulty hard harder hardest challenge challenges challenging "
    "complex complexity complicated confusing confusion problem problems issue "
    "issues trouble struggle tricky tough impossible unable lack lacking limited "
    "limitation limitations uncertain unclear unknown risky costly expensive".split()
)
CONNECTIVES = set("but however because since though although while yet so".split())
COPULAS = set(
    "is are was were be been have has had can may might could would should will must".split()
)

BASE = -0.06  # typical resting value
W_DIFFICULTY = -0.5  # the current word is a difficulty word
W_CONNECTIVE = -0.35  # a connective or copula/modal in the current position
W_AUX = -0.1
W_CONTEXT = -0.28  # per unit of decayed difficulty-word count
DECAY = 0.85  # how fast earlier difficulty words fade


def _word(token_string):
    return token_string.strip().lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # carry: (decayed difficulty count, document label) from the previous position.
    acc, last_doc = (0.0, None) if carry is None else carry
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if doc != last_doc:
        acc = 0.0  # a new document starts with no context
    word = _word(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    now_difficulty = word in DIFFICULTY
    value = BASE + W_CONTEXT * acc
    if now_difficulty:
        value += W_DIFFICULTY
    elif word in CONNECTIVES:
        value += W_CONNECTIVE
    elif word in COPULAS:
        value += W_AUX
    acc = acc * DECAY + (1.0 if now_difficulty else 0.0)
    return (acc, doc), float(value)

"""Weak, mostly-zero predictor for MLP unit 4276's down-projection component in layer 15.

What the component does: its activation is a small, diffuse signal (std about 0.43, almost
always between -1 and 1), with rare strong negative spikes in code (e.g. after `print`, or
around generic `<...>` and `::<` syntax). Its output direction promotes closing quotes and
string-ending tokens when negative, and closing parentheses when positive. No simple rule
here predicts the spikes or the bulk well.

What this program does: it sorts each token into a coarse character class (newline,
whitespace, digit, word, punctuation, other), and predicts that class's average activation
from the training rows. Words, newlines and spaced punctuation sit a little above zero;
unspaced punctuation and non-Latin text sit near zero. Measured on eval: variance explained
0.0027, correlation 0.05, and switching the component off costs the model almost the same
as this program does (kl_fraction 0.99). This captures only a sliver of the variance.
"""

READS = ()

# Mean activation per class, measured on training rows (rounded).
CLASS_MEAN = {
    "newline": 0.06,  # token holding a line break
    "space": 0.02,  # whitespace without a line break
    "digit": 0.03,  # a number token
    "word_sp": 0.0,  # a word starting after a space
    "word": 0.06,  # a word piece with no leading space (e.g. inside an identifier)
    "punct_sp": 0.05,  # punctuation after a space
    "punct": 0.0,  # punctuation with no leading space
    "other": 0.0,  # non-Latin text or a partial byte sequence
}


def token_class(s):
    if s == "" or "�" in s:
        return "other"
    if s.strip() == "":
        return "newline" if "\n" in s else "space"
    c = s.strip()
    if any(ord(ch) > 0x2E80 for ch in c):
        return "other"
    if c.isdigit():
        return "digit"
    if all(ch.isalpha() for ch in c):
        return "word_sp" if s[0] == " " else "word"
    return "punct_sp" if s[0] == " " else "punct"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, CLASS_MEAN[token_class(prefix.token_strings[-1])]

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 4279, read through one down_proj component.

The component is essentially one hidden unit of the layer-15 MLP: its input
weight is 0.87 on unit 4279 and near zero elsewhere, so its activation is that
unit's value. The unit goes strongly NEGATIVE on words that mean statistical,
logical or mathematical independence or separateness: "X is independent of Y",
"separate attributes", "unrelated", "orthogonal", "coprime" (gcd), "regardless",
"the processing of one request does not affect ...", and the Chinese 独立 / 无关 /
相干. It is weaker on "independent" in other senses ("independent school
district"). Its output direction suppresses those same words in the next-token
prediction, so a negative value promotes them.

This program: each concept word gets a strength (its typical negative activation
on the training text). The effect carries forward and fades by half per token,
and resets at each new document. The prediction is minus that strength.
It explains very little of the component's variance: most of its variance is a
dense background of small values (about +-0.35) on ordinary tokens, which no
word list captures.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Concept word -> typical size of the negative activation it produces.
STRENGTH = {
    "unrelated": 5.5,
    "disjoint": 4.8,
    "独立": 4.3,
    "independently": 3.9,
    "independent": 2.7,
    "separate": 2.3,
    "separately": 2.0,
    "orthogonal": 1.8,
    "mutually": 1.4,
    "validity": 1.5,
    "irrelevant": 1.3,
    "unaffected": 1.2,
    "gcd": 1.2,
    "regardless": 0.9,
    "distinct": 0.9,
    "separated": 0.8,
    "affected": 0.6,
    "affect": 0.5,
    "independence": 0.5,
    "相干": 6.7,
    "无关": 12.7,
}

FADE = 0.5  # how much of the previous token's effect carries over


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """Return (carry, predicted activation at this position)."""
    h, last_doc = carry if carry is not None else (0.0, None)
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != last_doc:
        h = 0.0  # a new document starts with no context
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    h = max(h * FADE, STRENGTH.get(word, 0.0))
    return (h, prefix.document_ids[-1]), -h

What this program does: it predicts the component's typical value everywhere, a

"""

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4281.

What it does: this component is almost silent. Its activation is a small, diffuse
number (mean about 0.04, spread about 0.32) that does not follow the identity of the
current or previous token, nor the document, so no readable rule accounts for most of
its variance. Its clearest behaviours are two small groups of negative responses:
  - "first" and "given" in a "given name ... (first name)" pattern, the kind of line
    in name lists such as "given name: jacques ( first name)": strongly negative;
  - boolean and logical words ("true", "false", "&&"): mildly negative.

This program predicts those behaviours and otherwise predicts the average value:
  - 0 at the first token of each document (the component is exactly silent there);
  - -2.0 on "first" and -1.0 on "given" when "name" or "given" appears in the 12
    tokens before;
  - -0.3 on "true", "false" and "&&";
  - 0.04 (its mean) everywhere else.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN = 0.04
CUE_WORDS = ("name", "given")
TRIGGERS = {"first": -2.0, "given": -1.0}
BOOLEANS = ("true", "false", "&&")
BOOLEAN_VALUE = -0.3
WINDOW = 12


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    t = prefix.position
    new_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if new_doc:
        return carry, 0.0
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    if word in TRIGGERS:
        before = [s.strip() for s in prefix.token_strings[-WINDOW - 1:-1]]
        if any(w in CUE_WORDS for w in before):
            return carry, TRIGGERS[word]
    if word in BOOLEANS:
        return carry, BOOLEAN_VALUE
    return carry, MEAN


def main():
    """Print the program's values on a short example, for a quick look."""
    tokens = ["given", " name", ":", " jacques", " (", " first", " name", ")", " if", " x", " &&", " true"]
    print([round(step(None, _Prefix(tokens, i), {})[1], 2) for i in range(len(tokens))])


class _Prefix:
    """A stand-in for the scorer's prefix, for `main` only."""

    def __init__(self, tokens, position):
        self.token_strings = tokens[: position + 1]
        self.document_ids = [0] * (position + 1)
        self.position = position


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 4282 of Qwen3-1.7B.

What it does: it fires on the token that introduces a value after a label.
The strongest cases are a colon after a field name ("Country:", "Last Modified:",
"given name:"), a JSON key's closing '":', a full-width colon, and the separators
' |', ' —', ' ->' and '=' in "name | property" tables and assignments. Colons
right after a number (times like 12:30, ratios) are weak, and every other token
is near zero.

The program keeps, for each document, which labels have already appeared. A label
seen before in the same document (so its value is a repeat the model can copy)
gives a smaller activation: 1/(1+n) after n earlier uses.
"""

READS = ()

# How strongly each separator introduces a value, in typical activation units.
SEPARATOR_STRENGTH = {
    '":': 11.0,  # closing a JSON key: "name":
    "：": 9.9,  # full-width colon
    ":": 8.5,  # colon after a label
    ":\n": 5.8,  # colon at the end of a line
    "=": 4.6,
    " ->": 5.5,
    " :": 4.7,
    " —": 4.0,
    " =": 3.6,
    " |": 3.8,
    ' "': 2.2,
    "':": 5.8,
    '):': 4.0,
    ' ==': 3.3,
}
DIGIT_FACTOR = 0.3  # separator right after a digit (a time, a ratio)
BASELINE = 0.07  # every other token sits near zero


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    seen = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else {}
    if prefix.position == 0:
        seen = {}
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    strength = SEPARATOR_STRENGTH.get(token, 0.0)
    value = 0.0
    if strength:
        label = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if prefix.position > 0 else ""
        uses = seen.get(label, 0)
        value = strength / (1 + uses)
        if label[-1:].isdigit():
            value *= DIGIT_FACTOR
        seen[label] = uses + 1
    return (doc, seen), 1.2 * value + BASELINE

"""A count-context unit: layer 15 MLP hidden unit 4283 (the down_proj component).

In plain terms: this unit goes negative in text that has just stated a quantity of
things ("284 references", "33 patients", "out of 14 cases, ..."). Its most negative
values come right after a count noun, and it is mildly negative on the commas,
brackets and linking words ("which", "including", "of", "with", "were") that follow
a number. Everywhere else it sits near a small positive baseline. Its variance is
mostly spread over contexts this program does not see, so the rule explains little.

The program reads only the text so far. It tracks how many tokens ago the last
number was, within the current sentence, and predicts:
- within 8 tokens after a number:
    a count noun (people, patients, years, ...)     -0.7
    another plural word                             -0.16
    a comma, bracket, conjunction or linking word   -0.15
    any other word                                  +0.035
- otherwise                                         +0.06
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping
import re

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Number words, and digits in any token, mark a number.
NUMBER_WORDS = frozenset(
    "zero one two three four five six seven eight nine ten eleven twelve twenty "
    "thirty forty fifty hundred thousand million billion dozen".split()
)
# Nouns that count people, patients, periods, things.
COUNT_NOUNS = frozenset(
    "people patients students years children points cases tests days items "
    "participants women men subjects samples studies countries teams weeks months "
    "hours words characters books games".split()
)
# Clause boundaries and the words that break a count down ("of which", "including").
LINKERS = frozenset(
    [",", "，", "(", "（", "and", "but", "or", "which", "including", "of", "with",
     "were", "these", "that", "in", "among", "total"]
)
SENTENCE_END = (".", "!", "?", ";", "\n")
WINDOW = 8


def _is_number(text: str) -> bool:
    word = text.strip().lower()
    return any(ch.isdigit() for ch in word) or word in NUMBER_WORDS


def _is_plural(word: str) -> bool:
    return bool(re.fullmatch(r"[a-z]{3,}s", word)) and not word.endswith(("ss", "us", "is"))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # carry: tokens since the last number in this sentence (None if there is none).
    new_document = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    since = None if new_document else carry
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = text.strip().lower()
    number = _is_number(text)

    near_number = since is not None and since <= WINDOW and not number
    if not near_number:
        value = 0.06
    elif word in COUNT_NOUNS:
        value = -0.7
    elif _is_plural(word):
        value = -0.16
    elif word in LINKERS:
        value = -0.15
    else:
        value = 0.035

    if number:
        nxt = 0
    elif since is not None:
        nxt = since + 1
    else:
        nxt = None
    if any(mark in text for mark in SENTENCE_END):
        nxt = None
    return nxt, float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 4284 (through one rank-one component of down_proj).

What this component is: almost all of it (about half its weight energy) is MLP hidden
unit 4284 of layer 15 itself, so its activation is a scaled copy of that unit. Its
output direction, read through the embedding, pushes toward and away from words such as
"として", "identity", "status", "nature": a negative activation promotes them, a positive
one suppresses them. Its activation is mostly small, with heavy tails in both directions.

What the program predicts: a rough, readable sketch of those tails.
- Strongly negative on Japanese kana (hiragana/katakana) and mildly negative on Han
  characters, which is where the big negative values cluster.
- Strongly negative on category or role nouns that complete a phrase like "as a ___"
  ("member", "instance", "agent", "tool", "gift", "threat", ...).
- Mildly positive on words that open a predicate or category slot ("a", "an", "as",
  "is", "considered", "important", "good", ...), and on the word after one.

Honest limit: this captures only a little of the variance (about 0.7% on held-out
training rows). Token identity alone would explain about 5%, and the rest is spread
over context that these word lists do not describe. The coefficients are least-squares
fits on training rows, rounded.
"""

import regex

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Words that open a predicate or category slot: "as a", "is an", "considered one".
PREDICATE_OPENERS = frozenset(
    {"a", "an", "as", "is", "are", "was", "be", "considered", "important", "good",
     "one", "just", "first", "not", "like", "most"}
)

# Nouns naming a role or category, which complete a phrase such as "as a member".
CATEGORY_HEADS = frozenset(
    {"member", "instance", "friend", "partner", "agent", "tool", "species", "resource",
     "threat", "gift", "participant", "optional", "example", "type", "kind", "form",
     "sort", "thing"}
)


def is_kana(text: str) -> bool:
    return bool(regex.search(r"\p{Hiragana}|\p{Katakana}", text))


def is_han(text: str) -> bool:
    return bool(regex.search(r"\p{Han}", text))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    same_doc = prefix.position > 0 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if same_doc else ""
    value = (
        -0.03
        - 0.61 * is_kana(word)
        - 0.16 * is_han(word)
        + 0.08 * (word in PREDICATE_OPENERS)
        - 0.62 * (word in CATEGORY_HEADS)
        + 0.06 * (prev in PREDICATE_OPENERS)
        - 0.05 * (prev in CATEGORY_HEADS)
    )
    return carry, float(value)

"""Component 4285 of layer 15's MLP down-projection: an "of" detector.

The component is strongly negative on the word "of" (and on the same
preposition in other languages: "de", "di", "van", "del", ...), the word that
ties a quantity or a part to the whole it belongs to: "a large number of
students", "some of them", "one of the", "30% of". Its size depends on the word
just before "of". After a quantity or fraction word ("all of", "most of",
"some of", "one of", "percent of") it is most negative; after an ordinary noun
it is moderately negative; after glue phrases ("because of", "instead of",
"out of", "consist of", "terms of", "instance of") it is only weakly negative.
"of" written without a leading space (after a newline or a symbol) is
weaker. Every other token gives 0, and the first token of a document gives 0.
"""
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Words that quantify or name a part of a whole: the "of" after them is strongest.
QUANTITY = set("few none several both some many most rest each three four two any all "
               "majority percentage portion fraction percent proportion subset half pair "
               "more much one group parts piece pieces %".split())
# Glue phrases where "of" is part of a fixed expression: the "of" is weak.
GLUE = set("because instead out instance consist consists consisting composed comprised "
           "capable regardless think terms way kind sort case place lack absence aware "
           "behalf care favor full heard rid exception thought made".split())
# The same preposition in other languages (partitive/genitive), a bit weaker.
OF_LIKE = {" de", " di", " del", " van", " von", " der", " du"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(prefix.token_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return carry, 0.0
    if word.strip().lower() == "of":
        if word != " of":
            return carry, -4.0
        before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()
        if before in QUANTITY:
            return carry, -10.0
        if before in GLUE:
            return carry, -2.5
        return carry, -7.0
    return carry, -2.5 if word in OF_LIKE else 0.0

"""Layer 15 MLP neuron-4286 readout, component 4286 of down_proj (a weak, mostly
unexplained signal).

What it does: this component's activation is almost entirely one hidden unit of
layer 15's MLP (neuron 4286) read out through the component's direction. That
unit has no clean token meaning: knowing the current token explains almost none
of its variance on held-out text, and so does knowing the previous token, the
next token, or any broad class (digits, punctuation, CJK, function words).

The one pattern found that is readable: path and directory separators in code
or shell text (e.g. "/", "/src", "__/", "/packages") push the activation clearly
negative. Every other token gets a small constant near the mean.
"""

READS = ()

PATH_BIAS = -0.2  # mean activation on path / directory separator tokens
BASE = -0.025  # mean activation on all other tokens


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    return carry, PATH_BIAS if "/" in token else BASE
